import requests
from datetime import datetime

# Get shifts for December
response = requests.get(
    ''https://xueqvozgeebhlffxmiqp.supabase.co/rest/v1/shift_requirements'',
    params={
        ''select'': ''id,start_time,end_time,headcount_needed'',
        ''start_time'': ''gte.2025-12-01'',
        ''start_time'': ''lte.2025-12-31'',
        ''order'': ''start_time''
    },
    headers={
        ''apikey'': ''$SERVICE_KEY'',
        ''Authorization'': ''Bearer $SERVICE_KEY''
    }
)

shifts = response.json()
print(f''Total shifts in December: {len(shifts)}'')
print()

# Group by date and calculate hours per shift
from collections import defaultdict
shifts_by_date = defaultdict(list)

for shift in shifts[:20]:  # Show first 20
    start = datetime.fromisoformat(shift[''start_time''].replace(''+00:00'', ''''))
    end = datetime.fromisoformat(shift[''end_time''].replace(''+00:00'', ''''))
    duration = (end - start).total_seconds() / 3600
    date_str = start.strftime(''%Y-%m-%d'')
    
    shifts_by_date[date_str].append({
        ''start'': start.strftime(''%H:%M''),
        ''end'': end.strftime(''%H:%M''),
        ''duration'': duration,
        ''headcount'': shift[''headcount_needed'']
    })

print(''Sample shifts (first 3 days):'')
for date, date_shifts in sorted(shifts_by_date.items())[:3]:
    print(f''\n{date}:'')
    for s in date_shifts:
        print(f''  {s[""start""]}-{s[""end""]} ({s[""duration""]}h) x{s[""headcount""]} people'')
